key_insight: The paper decomposes multi-agent prompt optimization into temporal and structural credit assignment so LLM systems can pinpoint which rounds and which agents are causing failures.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more sample-efficient, interpretable way to tune multi-agent LLM workflows by updating only the weakest links instead of doing broad black-box search.
method: Temporal credit: use state-space bottlenecks to identify critical rounds in the interaction trajectory.
Structural credit: use stationary role policies to isolate each agent’s contribution to the outcome.
Optimization: alternate verbalized block coordinate descent over role prompts and aggregation protocols with LLM-generated proxy gradients.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation across diverse reasoning benchmarks, showing lower query complexity while improving performance.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable proxy gradients and decomposed credit signals, which may be sensitive to prompt design and harder to stabilize in complex MAS settings.
paper_title: Unifying Temporal and Structural Credit Assignment in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Prompt Optimization
